interactions.title: The Magistros receives reports and breaks the monopoly
lines: DM: Okay. So… We start… jumping back in time… as… the Magistros of Chardon. What was his name again? Mitus Verina Auratan paces back and forth in a small chamber looking at maps. Late at night, and as he… drifts off to sleep, he gets a message.

DM: Sorry, as he drifts off to sleep, he's standing pacing with Tristan, the Windcaller, who casts a spell, and as he drifts off to sleep, he speaks with… Sorry, Tiberius. He speaks with… I'm just forgetting all the names here.

DM: He speaks with Tristan Brighteyes, the Windcaller who is traveling with you, who tells him that you are moving quickly across the Yeraad River Basin and should be arriving in the Chataan Mountains shortly. And from everything he's seen, he's never seen a… more… confident and put-together group of adventurers and is quite sure that the Chalyte Giant will be… defeated shortly.

DM: And a day passes. And another message… We've made it into the mountains. They just came back from scouting, it sounds terrifying. There's a… massive lightning tower suspended in air. From the lightning tower, thunder rings everywhere.

DM: The dwarf artificer Faldrak, his name, the captain of this ship, refused to get close, he… dropped off the… four of them off, actually. Five of them, because… one of them, Seeker, has a… copy of himself that walks around calling itself Seeker 3, not Seeker 2 for some reason. And… Faldrak, anyway, the captain, said he had to retreat and flew back 30 miles till we could just hear the distant echoes of the thunder.

DM: But they came back, in high spirits, saying they had suborned an ogre and got it to believe in a magic rock controlling its destiny. Which seemed impressive, but even better, managed to speak to a… a giant who apparently was willing to help, at least to the extent of, keeping the… ogre miners from spilling out of the mine and attacking them.

DM: And they seem excited to… teleport into the tower tomorrow, and… destroy this massive death ray. I don't know, Seeker the Dwarf, he says he can teleport anywhere in the world, he's never failed. Very impressive.

DM: And then… skipping ahead… The Magistros standing, with a few… advisors, Tiberius, the Windcaller, and a handful of others around noon, talking seemingly anxious, looking at each other, looking at the sun, wondering until… A message arrives, just a few words. Giant killed. Chalyte death ray destroyed. Chalyte is yours.

DM: And cheering erupts as… plans are put into motion quickly. The Magistros sends… immediately, messengers out accusing his own family of corruption, and enabling Fausto, through a dedication to personal profit and greed over the good of the citizens of Empire.

DM: Announces that all four of the Chalyte families are in breach of the conditions of the Chalyte monopoly granted to them, having allowed Fausto to possess and control large quantities of unlicensed chalyte. And that, from now on, processed chalyte will only be produced by the Windcallers or by others that they license. Anyone found in possession of Chalyte without a Windcaller license would be exiled.
DM: As these runners… travel across the city, launching the Magistros' plan into action.

before: Delwath: Get…
DM: Serious landlord mode going.
after: DM: Cut back to the edge of a giant crater in the mountains, full of the rubble of a massive tower and… full of… chaos. Ogres fleeing everywhere. Giants standing around trying to bring some order to the scene as one of them approaches you, speaking to the party. This is Brunnar, the one you spoke to before.

DM: The giants that survived, he says, are leaving the area. We will not linger long, he says, as those who are not dead are desperate to be free of the memories of this place. The ogres are your problem now, but we will bring to justice the remaining Chalyte sorcerers who worked for… Dhrukmir.
DM: All that the giants ask, he says, is to be left alone.

DM: Many of the stone giants, Brunnar says, fled east across the Myraeni Gap to the western edge of the Sentinels when Dhrukmir took over. And some will go try and find them. Others may remain in Ulgrathar, what they call this area of the mountains. And many stone giants prefer a solitary life.
DM: The chalyte is yours. We care not for what is here. And again, he says, all that we ask is leave us be.

DM: I'm glad I reached you.

DM: A few hours ago, a rider came… from the north. Place called the Alliance of Aurbez. You know this? It's north of us, if you follow the Dunmar-Maseau Road up towards Sembara. Maybe you passed through there when you were traveling south some years ago?

DM: The news was not good, and there was a letter addressed specifically to you. I told the rider I would send it along, but he said… no, Marcella would kill me if you didn't open it and read it directly, given that you apparently had some magic means of communication. So, I read it to you now.

DM: Dear Wellby and companions: I knew you had a good soul when you helped me flee Kadmos, and the rumors of your deeds since have only confirmed what I saw then. The tales we have heard in the Alliance Lands are garbled and fantastical, and I’m not sure I believe it all. But if even half of it is true, I hope you will hear my plea. Now, I have no right to ask more of you, for you gave me a new life I never could have had otherwise, a new family and a new home.

DM: I write now in terror, for this new home I have built on the Aurbez Plateau among the rangers and the generous, kind souls who have built a life on this harsh but beautiful land is threatened. Last night, a scouting party returned from deep in the Plaguelands with frightening news of a large Hobgoblin army on the march, heading for us. We know not when they will reach alliance lands, but our leaders fear the worst. It may be as little as 2 weeks until they are on our doorstep, though we pray for more time to prepare.

DM: Already the militias are mustering, and calls for aid have gone out on fast horses in all directions. We will not meet them unprepared, but barring some miracle, I fear our brave but untrained farmers and herders have little hope against such a force. I have heard stories of you sailing through the air in a ship made of stone and instantly appearing where you are needed in the blink of an eye. I pray that if ever legends were true, it is these that be so. Please help us, with all haste, if you possibly can.

DM: The Refounded Alliance of Aurbez needs whatever aid it can get. I know not where I will be when you get this letter. I hope it reaches you. But you can seek news at Aursenbourg, where there is some hope the newly built walls will hold back the danger, and at any of the watchtowers along the escarpment of the plateau.
DM: I write to you in desperation and fear, and pray the eight divines find a way for your… for my message to reach your hearts. In all faith and hope, Marcella. July… 29th.

DM: I spoke to the messenger, Sura says. He had ridden… fast and hard over the passes. Two horses lame. Riding across the monsoon… plains north of here. And as I said, just reached us just hours ago. This… news is already… more than 8 days old.

DM: I am… mustering what troops I can, but… there's no way we can cross the mountains in… 6 days, or less. I fear that we will just ride upon a… hobgoblin-ridden wasteland. I know a few people who could cover that ground that quickly.
